title: Comparing and Ordering Dissimilar Fractions
seo_title: Grade 4 Comparing Dissimilar Fractions Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Represent dissimilar fractions, with denominators up to 10, using models; compare dissimilar fractions using the symbols =, >, and <; order dissimilar fractions from smallest to largest, and vice versa.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets on comparing and ordering dissimilar fractions for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: models, common denominators, ordering and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rename with a common denominator, then compare the numerators.
key_sub: Same numerator: smaller denominator, bigger fraction.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Dissimilar fractions have different denominators, like 23 and 34.
  • Same numerator: the fraction with the smaller denominator is bigger (the parts are bigger).
  • Different numerators and denominators: rename both with a common denominator, then compare the numerators.
  • Benchmarks help: compare each fraction with 12 or 1.
  • Only compare fractions of the same whole.

Examples

Example

23 ☐ 34

812 and 912

8 < 9

Answer: <

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
A bigger denominator is bigger18 < 15: eighths are smaller parts.
Comparing only the numeratorsRename with the same denominator first.
Different wholesHalf of a big pizza is more than half of a small one.

items.q: Which number can be a common denominator for 34 and 56?
items.e: A common denominator must be a multiple of both 4 and 6. 12 = 4 × 3 and 12 = 6 × 2. Adding the denominators (10) does not work.

items.q: Which number can be a common denominator for 12 and 35?
items.e: A common denominator must be a multiple of both 2 and 5. 10 = 2 × 5 and 10 = 5 × 2. Adding the denominators (7) does not work.

items.q: Which number can be a common denominator for 23 and 34?
items.e: A common denominator must be a multiple of both 3 and 4. 12 = 3 × 4 and 12 = 4 × 3. Adding the denominators (7) does not work.
